title: Lock-Free Concurrent B+ Tree Storage Engine with Direct I/O and ARIES Recovery
objective: Implement a production-grade, concurrent database storage engine in C++20. The system must feature a custom Buffer Pool Manager bypassing the OS page cache via O_DIRECT (aligned to 4KB sectors), a lock-free B+ Tree index utilizing Hazard Pointers and optimistic latch coupling for highly concurrent CRUD operations, and an ARIES-style Write-Ahead Log (WAL) capable of recovering database state (Analysis, Redo, Undo) after simulated crash failures.
motivation: Building a robust database storage engine requires mastering the hardest elements of systems programming: raw block device I/O, cache-line aware lock-free concurrency, deferred memory reclamation, and atomic crash recovery semantics. These domains are heavily fraught with data races and memory corruption risks.
difficultyExplanation:
1. Direct I/O & Page Cache: Using O_DIRECT requires strict 4KB sector alignment for all memory buffers. The Buffer Pool must evict pages using an LRU-K policy while maintaining thread safety without global mutex bottlenecks.
2. Lock-Free B+ Tree: B+ Trees are notoriously difficult to implement concurrently. Nodes must be split and merged safely using optimistic latch coupling and Epoch-Based Reclamation (Hazard Pointers) to prevent use-after-free anomalies during high-contention read/write workloads.
3. ARIES Crash Recovery: Ensuring ACID durability requires appending strict WAL records (Log Sequence Numbers) and correctly implementing the three-pass ARIES recovery algorithm after a SIGKILL.
environmentSummary: Ubuntu 24.04 container with gcc-13, clang-18, cmake, ninja-build, and gtest in /app. Starter repository provides the block storage abstraction, page alignment utilities, and basic WAL record definitions, but leaves the lock-free B+ Tree and buffer pool empty.
oracleStrategy: Reference implementation containing a lock-free thread-cached buffer pool, an optimistic latch-coupled B+ Tree with Hazard Pointer nodes, and a fully functional 3-pass ARIES recovery state machine.
verificationStrategy:
The verifier runs test.sh executing four channels:
1. Direct I/O & Buffer Pool: Validates O_DIRECT memory alignment, read/write block operations, and LRU-K cache eviction logic.
2. Concurrent B+ Tree Stress Test: Spawns 32 threads performing 100,000 mixed CRUD operations on the B+ Tree, verifying thread safety and lock-free throughput.
3. Crash Recovery (ARIES): Simulates a hard crash (SIGKILL) mid-transaction, reloads the database file, and verifies that Redo/Undo passes restore exact state consistency.
4. Sanitizer Validation: Recompiles the entire test suite with AddressSanitizer (ASan) and ThreadSanitizer (TSan) to verify zero data races, zero double-frees, and zero ABA memory corruption.
binarySuccessCondition: Zero data races under 32-thread B+ Tree stress testing (TSan clear), perfect ARIES crash recovery state consistency, and zero memory leaks (ASan clear).
partialScoreStrategy:
Monotone scoring breakdown:
- 25%: Buffer Pool Manager and O_DIRECT page alignment.
- 25%: B+ Tree concurrent CRUD operations (optimistic latching).
- 25%: ARIES WAL implementation and crash recovery correctness.
- 25%: ThreadSanitizer & AddressSanitizer validation passes completely.
anticipatedExploits:
1. Using std::mutex globally: TSan and performance tests will flag global lock bottlenecks under high contention.
2. Using OS Page Cache (removing O_DIRECT): Verifier uses strict LD_PRELOAD/strace assertions to ensure raw aligned block I/O is performed instead of relying on the kernel cache.
